blocks.html: Lead Velocity Rate (LVR) is a growth metric that measures the month-over-month increase in qualified leads, indicating future revenue potential and pipeline momentum.

Lead Velocity Rate is a forward-looking performance indicator used to evaluate how quickly a business is growing its pool of qualified leads. Unlike revenue-based metrics, which reflect past performance, LVR focuses on pipeline expansion and helps predict future sales outcomes. It is widely used in B2B organizations to measure the effectiveness of marketing and demand generation efforts.
LVR is calculated by comparing qualified leads from one month to the next using the formula:

items.title: (Current Month Qualified Leads − Previous Month Qualified Leads) ÷ Previous Month Qualified Leads) × 100
Qualified Leads
items.html: include MQLs or SQLs based on company definitions

blocks.html: This metric is typically tracked monthly to monitor pipeline momentum and consistency of lead generation efforts.
Provides early visibility into revenue growth potential
Helps measure marketing and sales effectiveness
Supports more accurate forecasting and planning
Aligns demand generation with business goals
A company increases its qualified leads from 150 in May to 180 in June. This results in a 20% Lead Velocity Rate, signaling positive pipeline growth.

Lead Velocity Rate is a critical growth metric that helps businesses understand how quickly their qualified pipeline is expanding. By tracking LVR, organizations can better predict future revenue and optimize their lead generation strategies.
